question: Should OpenClaw define a universal agent-origin attestation, expose only a generic plugin-owned signing seam, or leave authentication to dedicated service plugins and tools?
rationale: This choice determines what the signature means, who owns keys and verification, privacy and replay guarantees, and which outbound request paths are supported.

options.title: Service-owned plugin authentication
options.body: Use a dedicated plugin or custom tool whose service owns keys, claims, audience, verification, and domain policy.

options.title: Generic signing seam
options.body: Expose a narrow allowlisted hook for OpenClaw-controlled HTTP clients without defining a universal OpenClaw identity.

options.title: Core attestation standard
options.body: Define and maintain an OpenClaw issuer, key lifecycle, claim format, replay protections, and explicit cross-path coverage.

recommendation.title: Service-owned plugin authentication
recommendation.body: Use a dedicated plugin or custom tool whose service owns keys, claims, audience, verification, and domain policy.
